subject: Private deployment network review & streaming SLOs — next steps
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Timothy Lau <tim.lau@arkwell.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Private deployment network review & streaming SLOs — next steps

Hi Timothy / Priya,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking us through Arkwell's inference flow. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps so we can lock the acceptance criteria for the private deployment performance run (scope: VPC gateway + VPN peering into customer-controlled subnet).

Key SLOs (proposed):
- Request p95 latency budget (end-to-end, app -> model) = <= 150 ms for single-request (non-streaming) workloads
- Streaming: token emission latency objetivo (server-to-client) p95 <= 60 ms for steady-state streaming; initial token (cold start) p95 <= 180 ms
- Concurrency: support 200 concurrent streaming sessions per RedWood gateway instance; overall initial target for your pilot = 200 concurrent sessions across the private cluster
- Throughput: sustained 20k tokens/sec aggregated across connections during peak window (burst up to 30k tokens/sec for < 2 minutes)

Network-specific constraints we noted:
- Traffic will egress through Arkwell NAT / private gateway. We need a list of egress IPs and NAT timeouts.
- Path MTU and TCP window sizing matter for large response batches — we'll include a PMTU run in the smoke test.
- VPN keepalive / idle timeouts: confirmation required (avoid KV cache GC during idle streaming).

Proposed immediate deliverables:
1) Arkwell provides VPC topology diagram (attached we annotated one from today) and list of egress IPs + maintenance windows (attachment: arkwell_vpc_topology.png).
2) Redwood provides a targeted net-SLO proposal and smoke-test plan (attachment: redwood-net-slo-proposal.pdf).
3) Technical deep-dive (1.5 hr) — suggested slots: Thu 12/2 10:00-11:30 PT or Fri 12/3 14:00-15:30 PT. We need Arkwell network/SRE + security + your infra lead for this.
4) Test window: 24-hour isolated run where Arkwell routes a mirrored traffic slice to our private gateway for measurements (we'll provide iperf/traceroute endpoints and client simulators).

Immediate asks for you by EoD Wed: egress IP list, VPN peer configuration (IKE version, encryption, DPD/keepalive), and a preferred deep-dive slot.

Attachments: arkwell_vpc_topology.png (image/png)

Thanks — I’ll sync with Karthik and Marissa on the test plan once we have the topology.

—
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Tim — good questions, answered inline (and copied Karthik for technical confirmation):

- Measurement point: p95 <= 150 ms should be measured end-to-end at the application ingress (your LB) to the Redwood gateway (so it includes the customer network hop to our gateway, but excludes client-side browser processing). For clarity, we will produce a measurement report showing both (a) customer LB -> Redwood gateway (network+gateway) and (b) gateway -> model (inference) so we can split attribution.
- Streaming token latency: server-to-client emission measured at the gateway (time between token ready in runtime and packet on the wire to your LB). We will include an e2e column in the report to show client impact if you run a mirrored client simulator.
- Ports/IPs: We'll need outbound access from the Redwood test client to your endpoints on TCP 443 (TLS) and UDP/ephemeral for ICMP/iperf runs. For our load generator we will supply a set of source IPs (you can allow them temporarily).

Action items and owners: 
- Arkwell (Tim/Priya): provide egress IP ranges, VPN/peer config (IKE details + DPD/keepalive) and preferred deep-dive confirmation (Fri 12/3 14:00 PT) — due EoD Wed 12/1.
- Redwood (Rachel/Karthik): share iperf/traceroute endpoints, load-generator IPs, and redwood-net-slo-proposal.pdf (attached).

Attachments: redwood-net-slo-proposal.pdf (application/pdf)

Looking forward to the deep-dive Friday. Karthik — quick note to you: once they provide egress ranges we should validate MTU, SYN/handshake RTT distribution, and expected NAT timeouts before the smoke window.

—
Rachel

Tim / Rachel / Priya — technical plan for the 24-hour smoke test and what we will measure (high level):

Smoke-test checklist:
1) Connectivity & path validation
   - Traceroute from Redwood load-generator to Arkwell LB and from LB to gateway; capture per-hop latency and MTU.
   - Path MTU discovery (PMTU) using icmp/probe to validate no fragmentation for 1500B payloads.
2) Bandwidth and sustained throughput
   - iperf3 sustained runs (3 x 10 min) to validate aggregate throughput; measure average and 95th percentile throughput.
3) Latency distribution (one-way where possible)
   - Measure SYN handshake RTT, TLS handshake time, and first-byte times.
   - Synthetic single-request p50/p95/p99 from your LB to Redwood gateway. Goal: p95 <= 150 ms.
4) Streaming token latency tests
   - Open N concurrent websocket connections and stream tokens at realistic token rates; measure per-token emission latency on the gateway side (server-to-wire) and end-to-end if you mirror clients.
   - Run concurrency profiles at 50/100/200/300 sessions to map degradation curve.
5) NAT & idle behavior
   - Verify NAT timeouts: run idle connections for expected idle window and ensure KV cache retention aligns with your NAT timeout (we'll provide keepalive recommendations).
6) Failure/fallback validation
   - Simulate a degraded path (add 100 ms artificial delay) and check automatic fallback behavior — define thresholds where Redwood routes requests to hosted fallback (proposal: route fallback if measured p95 > 250 ms for > 2 minutes).

Data we need from Arkwell (short list):
- Egress IP ranges to whitelist (CIDR list).
- VPN/IKE config and expected DPD/keepalive timeouts.
- Any middlebox that terminates TLS (TLS-terminating LB) vs pass-through.
- Preferred 24-hr test window (we propose Sun 12/5 00:00 — 12/5 23:59 PT to minimize production noise).

Expected outputs from Redwood after test:
- Detailed CSV of per-sample latencies (traceroute, tcp/tls/first byte), token-emission latencies per stream, concurrency degradation curves, and a summary report mapping measured numbers to the SLOs above.
- A short runbook with fallback thresholds and suggested config tweaks (MTU, TCP window, keepalive).

Links: JIRA SUP-1234 (smoke test ticket) | Test doc: https://drive.redwood.com/arkwell/tests/smoke-plan

I'll prepare the load-generator IP list and an internal checklist for Friday's deep-dive.
